messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT: streaming.generate p95/p99 SLO breach detected in us-east-1. Alert: streaming_tail_slo_breach. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/3115551234

maya (oncall): taking pager — looking now. @devon can you confirm scope?

devon (eng-sre): on it. quick prometheus check -> p95 jumped ~620ms -> 1.4s, p99 2.8s -> 6.5s. spikes line up with config_fetch timeouts and an uptick in 429s from token-store.

ops-bot: [alert] https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/3115551234 details posted. Paging infra and db.

sanjay (infra): seeing controlplane configstore read latency spike: p50 ~30ms -> 450ms, errors 5xx rising. Network errors in az-a reported by cloudprovider.

katie (product): any confirmed customer impact? Support reported streaming sessions stall — is that the same?

maya (oncall): yes, support flagged ~15 customers with stalled streaming sessions (chatbots, RL replay pipelines). Severity escalated to S1 — SLO breach and customer impact. Paging infra owners.

devon (eng-sre): logs show two correlated signals: repeated "configfetch: timeout" and bursts of "rate_limit: 429" from token-store. quick prom query i ran: sum(rate(config_fetch_errors[5m])) by (type) shows spike at 15:12 UTC.

henry (db): investigating DB side — heavy reads against feature_flags and config_cache tables. Found a slow seq scan on feature_flags for streaming_service. Looks like missing index on (service, key). Running explain now.

sanjay (infra): suggestion: enable cached-config fallback for streaming routes while we stabilize, and scale controlplane replicas 3->6 to absorb load.

devon (eng-sre): agree on fallback. Also want to route streaming to fallback non-streaming path (micro-batching) to avoid tail stalls. Henry, can you do a quick index or do we need a safer workaround?

henry (db): index create is safest long-term. I can run a CONCURRENTLY index: 
```
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_ff_service_key ON feature_flags (service, key);
```
This will avoid table locks but will take ~20-40m given table size. I can kick it now.

maya (oncall): mitigation plan (proposed):
1) Enable cached-config fallback (ttl 300s)
2) Scale controlplane replicas 3->6
3) Flip router to streaming fallback -> micro-batched path
4) Kick off index creation concurrently
5) Customer comms and monitor p95/p99
Who takes which item?

devon (eng-sre): I'll take 1 & 3. Running rollout now. Commands below.
```
# enable cached-config fallback
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/configs/fallback -H "Authorization: Bearer $PA" -d '{"mode":"cache_only","ttl":300}'
# flip router to fallback path
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/router STREAMING_FALLBACK=true
```

sanjay (infra): scaling controlplane now: `kubectl scale deployment controlplane --replicas=6 -n controlplane` — starting.

ops-bot: autoscaler triggered, new pods provisioning (3 -> 6). Logs: controlplane pod startup 6/6 ready.

devon (eng-sre): rolled out router env var; rollout status shows 6/6 ready. Monitoring metrics.

maya (oncall): customer comms draft: "We're investigating streaming stalls affecting some sessions. Mitigations are in progress; partial recovery expected within 10-30 minutes. We'll update as we have more details." @katie please send to affected list.

katie (product): sent to affected customers and internal CSMs. Noted degraded streaming behavior and ETA. :thumbsup:

devon (eng-sre): metrics update: p95 down to ~420ms, p99 down to ~1.2s, config_fetch_errors trending down, token-store 429s subsided. Streaming stall tickets decreasing.

henry (db): concurrent index creation kicked off, progress ~15% after 10m. ETA ~25m. No locks observed.

maya (oncall): good progress. Oncall handoff note: if p99 > 2s for >15m escalate to infra lead @sanjay and DB @henry. Documenting timeline in incident doc.

devon (eng-sre): assigning postmortem owners: devon (triage lead), henry (db fix/verify), sanjay (infra scaling/backfill), katie (customer comms). I'll pin dashboards/logs: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/3115551234

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied and metrics improving. Incident moved to "monitoring". Keep thread open for postmortem notes and final RCA.
